title: Your character
hook: choosing one trait to work on for a year

segments.voice: Yesterday: your charity, a jar on the shelf, and sadaqah wider than money. Your line was regular giving.

"And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." That's how Pickthall renders a line in surah al-Qalam, spoken to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Of everything that could have been praised about him, his courage, his leadership, his patience in hard years, the verse praises his nature, his character. Someone once asked his wife Aisha what his character was like. Her answer, as Sahih Muslim records it: his character was the Qur'an. Not a summary of it. The Qur'an, walking around. Today, the hardest part of practice: choosing one trait to work on for a year.
screen: `A TREMENDOUS NATURE.` → `HIS CHARACTER WAS THE QUR'AN.` → `ONE TRAIT, ONE YEAR.`

segments.voice: In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet says the best of you are those with the best character. Of all the measures he could have picked, that's the one in this hadith. Now look at the week behind you. A school, a teacher, a mosque, a circle, a regular gift: none of these is the goal on its own. They're tools for becoming a certain kind of person. A ruling known by heart and a temper kept on a short leash are meant to belong to the same life. Why one trait? Character is slow work. Scholars of the inner life, such as al-Ghazali in his Revival of the Religious Sciences, describe treating a bad trait by practicing its opposite, deliberately, over and over, until the opposite starts to come naturally: the impatient person practicing waiting, the stingy one practicing giving. That's hard with ten traits at once. It's possible with one: patience, honesty, gentleness in speech, keeping promises, controlling anger. And the companion habit. The tradition calls it muhasabah, taking account of yourself. At the end of a day, a short honest look: where did my trait show up today, and where did it slip? No drama, no despair. Just a ledger, kept daily, the way you'd check a garden.
screen: `THE BEST IN CHARACTER.` · `THE WEEK'S TOOLS SERVE ONE GOAL.` · `PRACTICE THE OPPOSITE.` · `MUHASABAH: A DAILY LEDGER.`

segments.voice: Ask one honest question: which trait, if it grew in me this year, would make the people around me breathe easier? Not the one that sounds best; the one your family would choose for you. Let a word come, patience, gentleness, honesty, calm, then picture one moment this week where it was missing, without punishing yourself, and see the same moment with it present; if you pray, ask Allah for help with it in your own words.
Your character. Akhlaq, the habits of the heart that show in how you treat people, worked on one trait at a time. Today's word.
Your line: one trait. Practiced on purpose, checked each night, for a year. A week of building, done.

howItsDone: Muslims describe good character, akhlaq, as central to the faith, following the hadith that the best of people are those best in character; some choose one trait to work on, and practice muhasabah, a short daily self-accounting, to watch their progress.
